solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Traditional support for female team has finally become muddled

indicators.note: takes only the last letter of 'has'

blocks.note: to addle is to become confused

explanation.surface: A women's team whose tactics have got into a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides in plain sight: a side-saddle is the seat women traditionally rode on, so 'support for female' is literal, not sporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-saddle was the conventional saddle for women riders, letting them sit with both legs on one side.

clue.text: Half of capital raised without assistance

indicators.note: takes the first two of OSLO's four letters
in a down clue, lifting letters turns them upside down, so they read backwards

blocks.note: OS, the first half of OSLO, turned up
the other half of OSLO, left where it is

explanation.walkthrough: Only one half of the capital moves: OSLO becomes SO + LO once its front half is flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something solo is to do it alone, without help.

clue.text: Go slowly guarding old cavalryman

indicators.note: DRAG ON surrounds the letter, as a guard surrounds what it protects

blocks.note: to drag on is to proceed slowly

explanation.surface: An instruction to advance cautiously while escorting a veteran horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go slowly' is a two-word phrasal verb, and the container opens exactly at its word break, which is easy to miss when it reads as one idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, a type of cavalry soldier.

clue.text: Woman drinking beer with resolve in party game

indicators.note: the woman takes the beer inside her

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A woman with a pint in hand finds the nerve to join a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: The courage sense is British slang, as in 'he lost his bottle', and the surface's pub setting makes the word look like a container for the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin the bottle is a kissing game played at parties.

clue.text: Water creature gun dog disturbed

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A retriever put out by some animal in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Water creature' the thing that disturbs the dog, but it is the definition, and the dog itself supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The dugong is a large marine mammal, relative of the manatee.

clue.text: Where one might bet star wants girl around

indicators.note: the girl goes around the star

blocks.note: Vega, a bright star in Lyra

explanation.surface: A celebrity who wants a girlfriend on his arm, in a gambling town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' tempts you toward a celebrity; it is the astronomical Vega.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Nevada city's casino strip makes it the best-known place in the world to gamble.

clue.text: Block group of pipes in lodge

blocks.note: read as church music: on an organ, the set of pipes sharing one tone, drawn out by a knob

explanation.surface: Someone sealing up the plumbing in a cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: block, a set of organ pipes, and 'lodge' in the British sense of staying somewhere, as in 'stop at a hotel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop a hole is to block it; to stop somewhere is to lodge there.

clue.text: Expensive article, it is elevated in the Pope’s headdress

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters makes them read upwards

explanation.surface: A pricey item raised aloft within the papal crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string DEAR A IT is read upwards at once, so IT ends up at the top. The definition is an adjective phrase: tiaraed means crowned with a tiara.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiaraed means wearing a tiara, and the papal tiara is the Pope's triple crown.

clue.text: Prompt to include godless American biased information

indicators.note: PROD takes PAGAN inside it

blocks.note: a pagan lacks the recognised god

explanation.surface: A call to push atheist American misinformation.
explanation.walkthrough: The American letter is not part of what is held: it follows outside the container, and 'godless' works as an adjective meaning heathen.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information slanted to promote a cause.

clue.text: Scholarship abandoned by Republican tendency

indicators.note: the scholarship loses the Republican

explanation.surface: Academia deserted by conservatives, a trend.
explanation.walkthrough: The political surface makes 'tendency' sound like a party faction; it is the plain noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a leaning toward something is a tendency to favour it.

clue.text: Work in sonar converting higher-frequency emitter

indicators.note: OP goes inside the rearranged letters
SONAR's letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Technical work on sonar that shifts it to a higher pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all acoustics engineering; the 'emitter' is a singer with the highest voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano sings the highest notes, so produces higher-frequency sound.

clue.text: Pact held with Tibet mobilising for violent conflict

indicators.note: to mobilise is to set in motion, so the letters of the pact are put on the move into a new order

explanation.surface: A treaty with Tibet held while troops mobilise for war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held' looks like the verb of the treaty sentence, but its letters belong to the fodder along with PACT and TIBET.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitched battle is a fierce, full-scale fight.

clue.text: Some men from Asia possibly embracing golf

indicators.note: CONTINENT wraps itself around the G

blocks.note: Asia is one example of a continent
G is golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A few Asian men who might be keen golfers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asia possibly' signals a definition by example in the wordplay: Asia is one of a class, and the class name is what goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group of people, often troops, forming part of a larger body.

clue.text: A husband getting answer that’s surprising

explanation.surface: A husband receives a surprising reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation, so 'that's surprising' stands for the whole cry rather than an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Aha! is an exclamation of surprise or discovery.

clue.text: Shop merchandise even now not moving

explanation.surface: Goods on the shelves that are still not selling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes unsold goods, so 'not moving' reads as a sales complaint rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless.

clue.text: One trying to get copper coin from the past

blocks.note: read as a sunbather after a coppery skin colour, not someone after money
read as old British money: slang for the sixpence, withdrawn after decimalisation

explanation.surface: Someone chasing an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a skin colour here, so the first meaning is a sunbather; a tanner was an old British sixpence coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanner tries to turn their skin coppery; a tanner was the old sixpenny piece.

clue.text: On which bishop sits in cape sporting a red hat

indicators.note: the letters are playful, rearranging themselves

explanation.surface: A cardinal-like bishop seated in a cape and red hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The vestments paint a churchman, so 'sporting' reads as wearing; its job is to rearrange A RED HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedra is a bishop's throne, which gives a cathedral its name.

clue.text: Second to none, but strangely unvarying

indicators.note: the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Something unbeatable that is oddly dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second to none' is a stock phrase meaning the best; it must be broken apart after 'Second'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotone describes something without variation.

clue.text: Begin to understand polar explorer not starting working forwards

indicators.note: SCOTT loses his first letter

blocks.note: Captain Scott, Antarctic explorer, without the S

explanation.surface: An Antarctic explorer who stalls at the start before pushing ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Robert Falcon Scott led the doomed 1912 race to the South Pole; the two ONs are the same letters from two different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is to grasp something at last.

clue.text: Send a message on river quality

explanation.surface: Texting from the river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second. The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Texture is the feel or character of a thing, a quality.

clue.text: Perhaps Elgar’s Enigma’s beginning with D minor?

definitions.note: Edward was Elgar's first name; 'Perhaps Elgar's' points to a forename Elgar had

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of Enigma

blocks.note: a ward is a minor under a guardian

explanation.surface: A question whether Elgar's Enigma Variations opens in D minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'D minor' looks like a musical key, fitting the Elgar surface; split it into D and a minor, a young person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar composed the Enigma Variations, so Edward is his name.

clue.text: Stagger about with stone for top of rampart

indicators.note: 'for' in the sense of 'in exchange for', as in swapping one thing for another, so ST is put where R stood

blocks.note: first letter of rampart, taken out

explanation.surface: Staggering around with a stone to the top of a castle wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' looks like reeling about; it means amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the transitive sense: news that staggers you leaves you reeling with amazement.

clue.text: King entering Polish site for pilgrims

indicators.note: the king walks into the word as into a room, so R sits inside SHINE

blocks.note: to shine shoes is to polish them

explanation.surface: A king visiting a Polish place of pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Polish' look like the nationality; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a holy place that pilgrims visit.

clue.text: What’s two-thirds nine?

blocks.note: read as a fraction to be calculated, and meant as two of the three letters of a word
read as the number to be divided, and meant as IX, nine in Roman numerals

explanation.walkthrough: Arithmetic says two-thirds of nine is six, which is true, but the trick is that the last two thirds of SIX spell IX, Roman nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Six is two-thirds of nine, and two of SIX's three letters are IX, nine.

clue.text: What can improve smile a test photo misrepresented

indicators.note: the letters are shown in a false arrangement

explanation.surface: A trial snapshot that gives a false impression of someone's smile.
explanation.walkthrough: The photo surface makes 'improve smile' sound like retouching; the definition is the stuff on your brush.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothpaste whitens teeth, making a smile look better.

clue.text: Steering wheel of hard wood

explanation.surface: A ship's wheel made of hardwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard wood' reads as one word, hardwood; split it and 'hard' gives a single letter while 'wood' names a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is a ship's steering gear, its wheel or tiller.

clue.text: Very small kangaroo uncovered inside the womb

indicators.note: strip off the outer letters of the whole phrase

blocks.note: minute = tiny; its M is lost
roo is short for kangaroo; its last O is lost

explanation.surface: A tiny joey still in its mother's pouch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' works on MINUTE ROO as a single string, removing only its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase kept in English, used by doctors for anything happening before birth.

clue.text: The very thing involving new and improper trespass

indicators.note: to involve is literally to roll something up inside, so IT wraps around the N

explanation.surface: A fresh and improper intrusion as the key issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The very thing' is the IT of 'that's just it', a small word hiding behind a three-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used as a verb: both mean to go where you have no right to be.

clue.text: Left EU, taking up current place

indicators.note: to take something up is to absorb it, as a sponge takes up water, so L EU holds the I

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Britain left the EU and took up a place in the present.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brexit surface reads 'Left' as a verb; it is just the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'.

clue.text: Clergyman replacing verse with frequency. I’m hesitating, it’s a big ask!

indicators.note: F takes V's place in REVEREND

blocks.note: f is the symbol for frequency in physics, put in

explanation.surface: A vicar hesitating over a difficult request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A big ask' is usually a demanding favour; here it is a question put to a whole electorate.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum asks the whole electorate a question.
